President Droupadi Murmu successfully wrapped up her three-country European tour, which included talks to deepen bilateral cooperation in important areas including trade and tourism. On July 20, Murmu began her journey with a state visit to Moldova—the first by an Indian head of state—during which she spoke with her Moldovan counterpart, Maia Sandu, about all aspects of bilateral relations. Additionally, the two nations decided to deepen their collaboration in a number of areas of shared interest, such as agriculture, infrastructure and logistics, healthcare and pharmaceuticals, renewable energy, and innovation. Murmu spent July 21–22 in North Macedonia following his visit to Moldova. She is the first president of India to travel to this Southeast European landlocked nation. Murmu spent July 21–22 in North Macedonia following his visit to Moldova. She is the first president of India to travel to this Southeast European landlocked nation. In addition to discussing cooperation in important areas including tourism, hospitality, and filmmaking, both nations decided to boost bilateral trade during this visit. The topic was brought up during a meeting between President Murmu and her counterpart Gordana Sijanovska-Davkova, which was followed by discussions at the delegation level. She also spoke at the first meeting of the India-North Macedonia Business Forum and the Assembly of North Macedonia. On July 23, Murmu made his first trip to Romania as an Indian head of state in more than thirty years. During her visit, among other important areas of bilateral cooperation, Romania and India decided to quadruple trade over the next three years and bolster defense collaboration. She spoke with Nicusor Dan, her Romanian counterpart, about bilateral relations. On Friday, Murmu spoke at the India-Romania Business Forum in Bucharest, the nation's capital. He also had extensive talks with Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan about bilateral relations. Additionally, the president engaged with members of the Parliamentary Friendship Group between Romania and India. In Romania, there are more than 13,500 Indians, including about 10,000 laborers. Additionally, the Bucharest University of Economic Studies here awarded Murmu an honorary doctorate. The university's highest academic honor, "Doctor Honoris Causa," is given to notable individuals who have made outstanding contributions to scholarship, public service, and international collaboration. Before heading to the airport on Saturday, Murmu had a meeting with members of the Indian community. Bos , Worthy News Europe Bureau Chief reporting from Budapest, Hungary BUDAPEST ( Worthy News ) – Hungary’s Prosecutor General Bálint Gábor Nagy resigned Wednesday unexpectedly, saying the Prosecutor’s Office must never become “an instrument of political struggle” as political turmoil deepened. Nagy, Hungary’s highest-ranking prosecutor, said sustained attacks against him had exceeded the limits of acceptable public and professional debate, threatening the independence and credibility of the Prosecutor’s Office. He said he was resigning to shield the institution from what he described as a politically motivated conflict. Prime Minister Péter Magyar, who had repeatedly urged Nagy to resign in recent months, welcomed the announcement saying Hungary had been “freed from another puppet” of former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. “Gentlemen, who will be next?” Magyar wrote on social media platform Facebook. Start your day with Christian news and biblical encouragement from Worthy News. The resignation comes amid mounting political tensions following a series of high-profile investigations involving officials linked to Orbán’s Fidesz party. On Tuesday, investigators from Hungary’s Prosecutor’s Office raided a Fidesz data center as part of a corruption probe involving the National Cultural Fund (NKA), seizing party servers. FIDESZ RAID SPARKS OUTCRY Orbán condemned the operation as politically motivated, comparing it to the final years of Hungary’s communist Kádár era. He said the seizure had left Fidesz without internet access, digital communications, or access to internal party data. The former prime minister rejected allegations surrounding the National Cultural Fund, describing the investigation as a “staged procedure.” He argued that officials administering roughly 47 million euros (about $53 million) in government-approved cultural funding had done nothing wrong and suggested the probe was primarily intended to justify confiscating Fidesz’s servers. Orbán also claimed Hungary under the current government was “not a democracy, but arbitrary rule.” He insisted that former President Tamás Sulyok was the country’s last legitimate head of state and argued that subsequent presidential appointments would ultimately be judged by history as unlawful. Orbán also announced that János Bóka had been appointed the new parliamentary leader of Fidesz, saying he would build a strong and confident parliamentary group representing the party’s supporters. Speaking at the same news conference, Orbán voiced his full support for former Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó, who recently left Parliament to accept a senior position with Chinese electric vehicle and battery manufacturer BYD. Orbán said he remained convinced Szijjártó could continue serving Hungary’s interests outside politics. BYD APPOINTMENT UNDER SCRUTINY Separately, Hungarian media and other sources said investigators had carried out a search at the Hungarian operations of BYD after Szijjártó accepted his new position with the Chinese company. News about the raids came while Parliament’s National Security Committee also met behind closed doors to discuss potential security concerns surrounding Szijjártó’s appointment. Lawmakers questioned whether the former foreign minister, who had access to classified state information while in office, should now work for a company outside both NATO and the European Union. Participants later said the committee’s proceedings had been classified until December 31, 2051, preventing public disclosure of the discussions for the next 25 years. The developments have intensified political debate over Hungary’s national security, its relationship with China, and the government’s handling of former senior officials. POLITICAL CONFRONTATION ESCALATES Fidesz has described the raids as unprecedented since the fall of communism in 1990 and accused the government of political intimidation. The party published what it called a “Declaration of Resistance,” pledging to continue what it described as “a peaceful struggle” to restore Hungary’s democratic rule of law. The resignation of the country’s top prosecutor, the investigations involving Fidesz, and the scrutiny surrounding Szijjártó’s move to BYD highlight the increasingly bitter confrontation between Prime Minister Magyar’s government and Orbán’s Fidesz opposition. https://www.ebrd.com/home/news-and-event.text: EBRD Annual Meeting and Business Forum The Annual Meeting of the EBRD Board of Governors is a key strategic event shaping the Bank’s strategic, financial, and operational directions. It serves as a high-level platform for engagement with shareholders, donors, business leaders, civil society, and the media. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) held its 35th Annual Meeting and Business Forum in Riga, Latvia , on 5–7 June 2026 against a backdrop of rapid change in our world. This year’s theme — “Volatile to versatile — economies innovating in a changing world” — explored how our economies are adapting to new realities. Visit the event website for more details. We gathered in Riga, in the Baltic region, which exemplifies the way dynamic economies can achieve outsized impact through innovation, digitalisation and forward thinking. There we reflected on our 35 years of boosting prosperity in economies in transition. Amidst volatility we promote versatility, empowering economies to adapt and thrive. We do this by enabling the green transition, strengthening governance and advancing human capital and equality of opportunity together with a focus on the private sector, mobilising investment and combining it with business advice and policy reform. A model first deployed in Eastern Europe is now delivering results in many other regions, including new countries in Africa and in Iraq . At the same time, our support for Ukraine is unwavering. We continue to help it strengthen its economy and maintain the momentum which will drive future reconstruction and growth. 2026 Annual Meeting and Business Forum website Watch live video from 2026 Annual Meeting and Business Forum Opening/closing and Governors' statements 2026 Annual Meeting Proceedings Watch highlights from the 2026 Annual Meeting in Riga, attended by hundreds of government representatives, regional business representatives, business guests and media. "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine," the president wrote on his Truth Social network. Trump continued: "Both parties have agreed," before urging restraint from both Kyiv and Moscow: "Do not break it!" Zelenskyy: Energy ceasefire 'news for me' There was ‌no immediate ​confirmation ⁠from Moscow, but Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the news site Axios within minutes of Trump's post that the ceasefire was "news for me." "The ceasefire announcement was news for me. But if Russians agree to an energy ceasefire, Ukraine will agree. If President Trump negotiated it with Putin, please tell us when the ceasefire begins; we are ready and we will accept it," he told Axios . How Russia turned sanctions into a diesel deal To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video In a social media post later, Zelenskyy said a drone had hit a Kyiv power plant, leading to power outages in the capital. The Ukrainian leader had earlier repeated his stance that Ukraine would stop hitting Russian oil refineries if the Kremlin curbed its energy attacks. Trump and Zelenskyy have argued this week over Ukraine's attacks on Russian diesel facilities, which the US president said have contributed to a global diesel shortage, rather than the Iran war. Trump needs lower fuel prices before midterms Trump said Friday he had struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to buy diesel from Russia . The controversial move was an attempt to bring down high fuel prices ahead of the US midterm elections next month. However, this move undercuts fresh US sanctions Trump signed just weeks ago to further hurt Russian energy revenues funding the war. Backing Zelenskyy in the Trump row, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said that she "fully supported" the call for a "ceasefire that protects global food supplies and energy infrastructure in Ukraine and Russia." "And my full support for President Zelenskyy as he leads the fight for his people's freedom," she wrote online. On X, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said his country "strongly supports" Trump's call for a "sustained energy ceasefire to start now," which he said Kyiv was ready to honor "if Russia stops its attacks." French President Emmanuel Macron said his country backs a "real energy ceasefire," but lamented that "Russia continues to refuse that." After earlier denouncing the Trump-Putin deal, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he supported the energy ceasefire, in a phone call with Trump, his office said. War abroad, soaring prices at home: is Trump in trouble? Recently, Ukraine has stepped up long-range strikes deep inside Russian territory, targeting major oil refineries and other facilities to curb Moscow's refining capacity and fuel supplies. Kyiv on Sunday pressed on its campaign against Russian infrastructure, hitting a data center run by Russian technology giant Yandex. It was the third strike on the company’s facilities in four days. https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/141827.text: Russia warns it could use nuclear weapons if NATO cuts off Kaliningrad NATO rejected Moscow’s claims and said its activities do not threaten Russian territory Russia has warned NATO that it could use nuclear weapons if the alliance attempts to isolate Kaliningrad, its heavily militarised exclave on the Baltic Sea. According to Al Jazeera, a diplomatic document sent to NATO, Moscow claimed it had “information that NATO is preparing an air and naval blockade of Kaliningra.” Russia said it was prepared to use its entire military arsenal, including nuclear weapons, to defend the territory if NATO countries attempted to cut it off from the rest of Russia. NATO rejected Moscow’s claims and said its activities do not threaten Russian territory. Secretary-General Mark Rutte said NATO remained a defensive alliance and urged Russia to “stop the nuclear threats”. He also said Russian President Vladimir Putin “knows that he can never win” a direct confrontation with NATO. Kaliningrad sits between NATO members Poland and Lithuania and hosts Russia’s Baltic Fleet and nuclear-capable Iskander missiles. The warning comes amid heightened tensions in the Baltic region following alleged Russian airspace incursions and other military incidents. Poland has recently strengthened its air defences, while Denmark reported an encounter involving a Russian warship and Danish military helicopter.
